records.title: Active Defense: China’s Military Strategy since 1949
records.author_org: M. Taylor Fravel; Princeton University Press
records.date: 2019 copyright and cited hardback; recovered text also identifies first paperback printing in 2020
records.type: Historical scholarly monograph; exact cited pages recovered in a public university-hosted copy, with source limitations retained
records.description:
Fravel’s historical study traces changes in official military strategy from 1949. Campbell cites it repeatedly for historical interpretation, and Pollpeter cites it in contextualizing strategic writing. The publisher catalog identifies the edition.

Metadata correction from the original page. The index now gives a readable title and distinguishes original source, authors and editors. Earlier garbled titles and credit fields are retained in source_metadata_history. The original headline follows the concise English rendering in brackets. Individual passage findings and remaining gaps remain separately visible in the linked audits.

Citation-index repair. Shorthand notes 9, 30, 31 and 82 all refer to Fravel’s Active Defense, fully indexed in note 7. Their four omitted associations are restored to this existing work, while the old shorthand-row IDs remain valid. A recovered university-hosted copy has 2019 copyright and a 2020 paperback imprint. Exact historical pages were checked once for the group and separately compared with each citing passage. Some usages remain partial or require correction; a shared title does not give every claim the same verdict.

Individual contextual follow-up, November 17–22, 2026. The recovered book’s printed p. 218 / PDF p. 237 confirms the June 2004 policy adjustment, its informatization formulation and continuity in the broad areas of focus. The author’s later explanation on printed p. 222 / PDF p. 241 explicitly discusses learning from the 1999 Kosovo and 2003 Iraq conflicts, supplying the causal context not on the single cited page. The citation should include that additional locator. Fravel describes a limited adjustment rather than a wholly new strategy and states that the underlying decision documents were not public. The supported finding is an accurate account of this historical scholarly interpretation, with its documentary limits, not independent access to the internal decision or proof of implementation. The exact cited printed pp. 217–220 were checked in the recovered book, PDF pp. 236–239. The opening characterizes the 2004 change as a minor adjustment, and p. 220 gives the coordination-versus-integration distinction summarized by the report. The single-network formulation is Fravel quoting Dean Cheng, rather than a directly reproduced original Chinese guideline; that nested attribution is now explicit. The source’s own warning about limited decision-making documentation is retained. The conceptual historical comparison is supported, without treating a published organizational ideal as demonstrated field performance or providing procedures for implementing it. Fravel’s original book was recovered in a public university-hosted copy. The imprint gives 2019 copyright and first paperback printing in 2020; printed p. 139 is PDF p. 158. It supports the Soviet threat and the September 1980 adoption of a forward-oriented defense, contrasting it with the earlier strategy. The citing paragraph extends the formulation across both the 1970s and 1980s and adds U.S. collaboration as a causal setting. Those wider temporal and causal claims are not established on the specified page. The source explicitly asks why strategy changed only in 1980 despite the earlier threat, so the stages should not be flattened. The shorthand is linked to the already indexed full book, preserving its old row ID. This is historical attribution, not a modern operational prescription. The September 18, 2020 PLA Daily interview preserved on Yunnan News explicitly names Yang Xiaolun, 杨晓论, in its headline and identifies his historical commander role. This corroborates that role as of the 2020 interview. The bibliography’s English rendering Yang Xiao is incomplete relative to the Chinese name and should retain the final syllable. The separate December 29, 2019 source was attempted once for this and note 116 and returned HTTP 404. The recovered 2020 interview alone does not establish the exact start of his appointment or independently verify that he held the same position at every earlier event. The preceding statement about Li Zongli’s attendance has its own marker, note 122, and is not counted as verified by note 123. The four source components were separated and checked for the historical formation claim. The December 29, 2019 PLA Daily endpoint returned HTTP 404. The accessible September 2020 account and December 2022 retrospective identify the team and its activities but did not supply the claimed late-2017 establishment date in the historical passages examined. The May 1, 2022 Qilu report explicitly describes the team as just over four years old, which is compatible with a 2017 origin but does not establish the precise year-end date. A 2017 number in the website licensing footer is not an establishment year. The exact formation record and the unavailable 2019 article remain gaps. No operational methods or launch procedures are treated as verified by these historical checks. Only the historical more-than 90percent personnel statistic at supplied PDF p.20 was reviewed. Its exact 2019 PLA Daily source remains 404. The actual 2020 companion article does not supply the missing denominator/statistic; an unrelated 90th-anniversary sidebar is not evidence. The personnel category, date and claimed figure remain unverified. The report’s suggested causal link to training is additionally an inference, not established by a percentage alone. No technical training method was assessed. That original returns 404 and no matching body was recovered. The report’s later 2020 party-committee-secretary description is a different dated role and cannot retrospectively prove this 2019 office. Political commissar, party secretary and a department’s party-committee secretary are not automatically interchangeable offices. Preserve the report’s tentative inference and the missing appointment/passsage evidence. The formal organizational-category attribution at supplied PDF p.17 was checked against both cited PLA Daily works. The December 29, 2019 original is 404. The actual September 2020 article calls it a launch team, but its recovered body does not establish the specific formal launch-group label used by the report. A descriptive team name is not an establishment table. Preserve the historical source gap and the distinction between functional reporting and formal organizational status.

One yearly conference does not establish an uninterrupted annual series or prove every group in the broader report’s list participated every year. This check concerns the historical meeting record, not technical R&D priorities.
